topic.title: Running an Incremental Translation
topic.shortdesc: Describes what happens when you run the translation agent on a project.

body.p: When you start a translation job, the agent first works out the translation status of every source file covered by your selection, then translates only the files that need it. You follow and manage the job from its card, the same way as any other translation job; see Following and Managing a Translation Job.

section.title: Translation Status
section.p: Each source file has one of three statuses for a given target language:

ul.li: Missing - The file has never been translated into this language.
Stale - The file was translated before, but its English source changed since the last recorded translation.
Current - The recorded translation already matches the current English source.

section.p: The agent determines whether a file is stale by comparing the English file's current version against the source version recorded the last time its translation was updated, using the translation index. Current files are skipped entirely, which is what makes translation incremental.

section.title: How Files Are Processed
section.p: For a stale file, it uses the existing translated file as context when producing the updated translation, so previous phrasing and terminology choices carry over instead of being translated from scratch. A file is only marked as current once its translated file passes validation.

section.title: Manual Edits Are Preserved as Context
section.p: Hand-editing a translated file directly does not, by itself, make it stale; staleness is only about whether the English source changed. So a translated file you corrected by hand stays current until its English source changes again. When that happens and the file becomes stale, the agent reuses your manual correction as context for the next translation, so your wording is carried forward rather than retranslated.
